lectures.title: State Legislature: structure and the Legislative Assembly

parts.t: The State Legislature: constitutional framework
items: **Article 168:** The State Legislature consists of the Governor + Legislative Assembly (+ Legislative Council in bicameral States).
Governor + Legislative Assembly (Lower House) + Legislative Council (Upper House)
**6 Bicameral States (current):** Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Uttar Pradesh.
**Historical origin:** Bicameralism was first introduced in India at the Central level by the Government of India Act, 1919 (Council of State and Central Legislative Assembly).

**The term "Council":** In Indian Polity it spans three distinct constitutional institutions; one is the State Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad): Upper House of bicameral State Legislatures (Arts. 168, 169, 171).

parts.t: Legislative Assembly: nature and election
items: **Nature:** The Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) is the Lower / Popular House of the State Legislature (Art. 168); constitutional basis is Article 170.

**Electoral system:** Directly elected by the people (citizens of the State) from single-member territorial constituencies on the basis of Universal Adult Suffrage (Art. 326) using the First-Past-the-Post (FPTP) system.
**Electoral authority:** Elections to the State Legislative Assembly are conducted by the Election Commission of India (ECI) (Art. 324), NOT the State Election Commission.
**FPTP trap:** A candidate does NOT need an absolute majority (>50%); the candidate securing the highest number of valid votes wins.
**Collective Responsibility (Art. 164(2)):** The State Council of Ministers is collectively responsible specifically to the Legislative Assembly.
**Age qualification (Art. 173):** Minimum 25 years for Legislative Assembly (vs. 30 years for Legislative Council).

parts.t: Assembly strength: ceilings, floors and superlatives
items: **General limits (Art. 170):** Maximum = 500 members (seats); Minimum = 60 members (constitutional floor / minimum standard floor, subject to statutory exceptions).
**Sikkim Assembly:** Smallest State Assembly with 32 seats (less than the standard constitutional minimum of 60).

parts.t: Reservations in the Assembly
items: **SC/ST seat reservation (Art. 332):** Mandatory reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in every State Legislative Assembly in proportion to their population in the State (based on population ratios).
**104th CAA (2020):** Ended the nomination of Anglo-Indian members under Art. 333.
**106th CAA (2023):** Provides approx 1/3rd reservation for women in directly elected Assembly seats (effective after post-census delimitation).

parts.t: Presiding officers of the Assembly
items: **Speaker & Deputy Speaker (Art. 178):** Chosen/elected by the Assembly from amongst its own sitting members.
**Resignation (Art. 179):** The Speaker submits resignation to the Deputy Speaker; Deputy Speaker resigns to the Speaker.

**Continuation after dissolution (universal trap):** When the Assembly is dissolved, the Speaker does NOT vacate office immediately; continues in office until immediately before the first meeting of the newly elected Assembly.
**Voting:** Speaker cannot vote in the first instance, but exercises a casting vote in case of an equality of votes (tie).
**Money Bill status:** The Speaker decides Money Bill status.

parts.t: Tenure, sessions and the Governor's interface
items: **Term (Art. 172):** Normal term is 5 years (unless dissolved earlier); the Assembly is dissolvable / temporary.

**Emergency extension (Art. 172):** During a National Emergency (Art. 352), Parliament may extend the Assembly's duration by law for 1 year at a time, up to a maximum of 6 months after the Emergency ceases.
**Sessions & dissolution (Art. 174):** The Governor summons, prorogues, and dissolves the Legislative Assembly (maximum session gap: 6 months).
**Governor's Address (Art. 176):** Addressed at the commencement of the first session after each general election and the first session of each year.
**Assent and reservation:** Governor can reserve a State Bill for President under Art. 200; President considers under Art. 201.

parts.t: Disqualification of members
items: **Grounds (Art. 191):** Include holding an office of profit, unsound mind, undischarged insolvent, or loss of citizenship.
Must obtain the mandatory & binding opinion of the Election Commission of India (ECI) and act according to such opinion
Speaker in the Assembly; Chairman in the Council
Decided exclusively by the Speaker (subject to judicial review)
**Disqualification deciding head:** Art. 191 disqualifications: Governor acting on ECI's binding advice. Anti-defection under 10th Schedule: Speaker.

parts.t: Key Articles of the State Legislative Assembly

lectures.title: State Legislative Council and its comparison with the Assembly

parts.t: Creation and abolition of the Council (Article 169)
items: **1. State Assembly Resolution:** Initiated by the State Legislative Assembly passing a resolution by a Special Majority (≥ 50% / majority of total membership AND ≥ 2/3rd of members present and voting).
**2. Parliamentary Law:** Enacted into law by Parliament by a Simple Majority (like an ordinary bill).
**3. Article 368 Exclusion:** The creation or abolition of a Legislative Council is NOT deemed an amendment of the Constitution for the purposes of Article 368.
**Article 169 resolution trap:** The State Assembly resolution is recommendatory; it does NOT legally compel the Union Government to introduce a Bill in Parliament.

parts.t: Strength and nature of the Council
items: **Nature:** The Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is the Upper House / House of Elders; constitutional basis is Article 171.
**Maximum strength (Art. 171):** 1/3rd of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly.
**Largest Legislative Council:** Uttar Pradesh (100 members / seats).
**Permanent body:** Cannot be dissolved; 6-year member term; 1/3rd retire every 2 years.

parts.t: Composition and electoral quotas (Article 171(3))
items: Elected by the Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs) from non-MLAs
Elected by Local Authorities / Local Bodies (Municipalities, District Boards, etc.)
Elected by Graduates of ≥ 3 years standing residing in the State
Elected by Teachers of ≥ 3 years standing in educational institutions ≥ secondary school level
**Voting system:** Indirect election; elections are conducted via Proportional Representation by means of Single Transferable Vote (PR-STV) under secret ballot, plus nomination.
**Governor's nomination fields (5 categories):** Literature, Science, Art, Co-operative Movement, and Social Service.

**Trap:** Co-operative Movement exists under Article 171 for State Councils, but is NOT a nomination ground for Rajya Sabha under Article 80. "Industrialists" or "Commerce" are NOT valid categories (Industrialists are NOT an electoral category: BPSC trap).

parts.t: Chairman and the dissolution vs abolition trap
items: **Chairman (Art. 182):** Chosen/elected by the Council members from among themselves; the Governor does NOT nominate the Chairman.
**Defection decider in the Council:** Chairman (10th Schedule).
**Trap:** Statement claiming "Legislative Council can be dissolved on the recommendation of the Governor" is FALSE (it is a permanent body).
**Trap:** Statement claiming "Legislative Council cannot be abolished" is FALSE (can be abolished under Art. 169).

parts.t: Money Bills in the State Legislature
items: **State Money Bills (Art. 198, 199, 207):** Can originate ONLY in the Legislative Assembly, on the prior recommendation of the Governor (Art. 207).
**Certification:** The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly has sole and final authority to certify whether a Bill is a Money Bill.
**Council's role:** Receives the bill for recommendations only (recommendatory only) and must return it within 14 days (max detention: 14 days); it cannot amend/reject.
**Assembly's final authority:** Assembly is free to accept or reject any recommendation; bill is deemed passed upon expiry of 14 days.

parts.t: Ordinary Bills: the Council's delaying power (Article 197)
items: **First passage (first instance):** When the Assembly passes an ordinary Bill and transmits it to the Council, the Council can delay it for a maximum of 3 months.
**Second passage (re-passed by Assembly):** Council can delay for a maximum of 1 month.
**Total maximum delaying period:** 4 months (3 months 1st time + 1 month 2nd time).
**No veto:** The Legislative Council has no veto power and cannot permanently block an ordinary Bill passed by the Assembly; it can only delay it for a maximum of 4 months.

parts.t: Assembly vs Council: comparison
items: Dissolvable / Temporary; 5-Year Term; subject to dissolution
Permanent Body; 1/3rd retire every 2 yrs (6-yr member term)
Base constitutional House; cannot be abolished
Can be created/abolished under Article 169 (Assembly Special Majority + Parliament Simple Majority)
Introduced ONLY in Assembly (sole House of introduction); Speaker certifies; final authority
Recommendatory only; can only delay for 14 days (max detention); cannot amend/reject
Max total delay: 4 months (3 months 1st time + 1 month 2nd time)

parts.t: Legislative Council vs Rajya Sabha vs Legislative Assembly
items: Cannot be dissolved, but CAN be abolished (Art. 169)
Cannot be dissolved and CANNOT be abolished
Can be dissolved, but CANNOT be abolished
Chairman (Elected by Council from its members)
Speaker (Elected by Assembly from its members)

lectures.title: Centre-State legislative relations and the Seventh Schedule

parts.t: Key Articles on Centre-State relations
items: Subject-matter of laws (Union, State, Concurrent Lists)
Power of Parliament to legislate on State List in national interest

parts.t: Seventh Schedule: the three-fold distribution
items: **Constitutional framework:** Governed under Part XI (Articles 245–255) and the Seventh Schedule, operationalized through Article 246 (subject distribution) and Article 246A (special provision for GST via 101st CAA, 2016).
State Legislatures have exclusive legislative competence
Both Parliament and State Legislatures have concurrent legislative competence
**Residuary Powers (Article 248):** Legislative competence over any subject NOT enumerated in any of the three Lists is vested exclusively in Parliament (e.g., Space Research, Cyber Law).
**Residuary power locus:** In the USA and Australia, residuary powers lie with the States; in Canada and India, they lie with the Centre.

**Repugnancy Rule (Article 254):** In case of conflict between Central and State legislation on a Concurrent List subject, the Central law prevails (unless the State law was reserved for Presidential assent and received it under Art. 254(2)).

**GST Dual Competence (Art. 246A):** Gives simultaneous powers to both Parliament and State Legislatures to frame laws regarding Goods and Services Tax (breaking the strict exclusive-list dichotomy of Article 246).

parts.t: Subjects of the three Lists
items: List II: State List (State Legislature Exclusive)

parts.t: Placement traps in the Lists
items: Railways: Union List (List I); Railway Police: State List (List II, under "Police")
Police, Public Order, Prisons: State List (List II); Criminal Law & Criminal Procedure: Concurrent List (List III)
Corporation Tax: Union List (List I); Land Revenue: State List (List II)
Inter-State Trade & Commerce: Union List (List I, Entry 42); Price Control: Concurrent List (List III)
Trade and Commerce within State: State List (List II, Entry 26; subject to List III Entry 33)
Economic and Social Planning: Concurrent List (List III) (Trap: Not Union List); Census: Union List (List I)
**Local Self-Government placement:** Panchayati Raj and Municipalities are strictly enumerated in List II (State List, Entry 5).

parts.t: 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976: the five subjects shift
items: **Five subjects** were transferred from the State List (List II) to the Concurrent List (List III).
Protection of Wild Animals and Birds
Administration of Justice (Constitution and organisation of all courts except the Supreme Court and High Courts)
**Entry 20A:** The 42nd CAA also inserted Entry 20A: Population Control and Family Planning into the Concurrent List.

parts.t: When Parliament can legislate on the State List
items: Rajya Sabha Resolution in national interest (≥ 2/3rd members present & voting)
Resolution remains in force for 1 year; the law ceases 6 months after the resolution lapses.
Extends to whole or any part of India; ceases 6 months after emergency ends.
Request by ≥ 2 State Legislatures via resolutions
Law applies ONLY to consenting States; can be amended/repealed only by Parliament.
Plenary power to enact laws for implementing international conventions/accords.
Proclamation of President's Rule in a State
Parliament exercises the legislative powers of that State Legislature.

parts.t: Doctrines on legislative competence
items: Prafulla Kumar v. Bank of Commerce (1947) / State of Rajasthan v. G. Chawla (1959)
Resolves legislative field overlaps; examines the true nature and essence of a law rather than its incidental encroachment on another List.
Kameshwar Singh v. State of Bihar (1952)
"What cannot be done directly, cannot be done indirectly": transgression of legislative competence masked under a permissible guise.

lectures.title: Centre-State relations: commissions, Inter-State Council and Article 356

parts.t: Commissions and committees on Centre-State relations
items: Appointed by the Tamil Nadu Government to examine Centre–State Relations; State-level initiative for federal autonomy
Landmark commission; recommended a permanent Inter-State Council / Inter-Governmental Council (Art. 263)
NOT Centre–State relations: classic elimination option under Centre–State questions (key elimination trap)
**Punchhi Commission (core identity):** Second major Commission on Centre–State Relations and Indian Federalism.
**Punchhi Commission (mandate):** Appointed to review working, conventions, judicial interpretations, and dialogue mechanisms governing Centre–State Relations.
**Mentally categorized under:** Federalism -> Centre–State Relations -> Coordination & Dialogue Mechanisms.

**Sarkaria Commission (1988) & Punchhi Commission (2010):** Under the Ministry of Home Affairs, on Centre-State Relations & Regionalism; addressed federal tensions, deployment of central armed forces, inter-state council revitalization, and objective criteria for invoking Article 356.
**Punchhi vs Sarkaria trap:** Recommendation for a Permanent Inter-State Council / Inter-Governmental Council -> Sarkaria Commission (NOT Punchhi Commission).

parts.t: Inter-State Council (Article 263)
items: **Constitutional basis:** Article 263 (Constitutional body, NOT a purely non-constitutional/extra-statutory body).
**Established by:** President of India (NOT enacted/established by Parliament).
**Establishment date:** Formally set up on 28 May 1990 following the recommendations of the Sarkaria Commission.

parts.t: President's Rule and the Union's duty to protect States
items: **President's Rule (Art. 356) first imposed:** Punjab (1951); PEPSU followed in 1953.
Article 356 (President's Rule) subject to Judicial Review; Secularism is Basic Structure

**IMDT Act (Sarbananda Sonowal, 2005):** Illegal Migrants (Determination by Tribunals) Act struck down under Article 355 (Duty of Union to protect States against external aggression/internal disturbance).
